image_description: A medium shot of a young musician seated in an orchestra or band setting, holding a large wooden bassoon. The instrument is held diagonally across the body. Visible features include the long wooden boot joint and wing joint, metal keys, and the upper part of the instrument extending upwards. In the foreground right, another musician's profile and music stand are visible. Background shows blurred audience or other musicians.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument extends from the player's lap to well above their head, consistent with the ~1.3m height of a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is taken from a side/profile angle. While the U-shape structure exists physically, it is not visually distinct as a 'U' from this perspective; the parallel tubes overlap or appear as a single diagonal mass.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is invisible from the exterior view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The very top of the instrument where the bocal inserts is cut off by the top edge of the image frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple silver-colored metal keys and keywork mechanisms are clearly visible on the wooden body of the instrument.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument is held diagonally. The flare of the bell is partially visible at the top left, though the full opening is near the frame edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood exhibits the characteristic dark reddish-brown hue and polished reflection typical of maple bassoons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible keywork is silver-colored nickel silver or silver-plated.
The main body segments (boot and wing joints) are clearly constructed from turned wood.

artifact_observations.location: Sheet music on stands in foreground and midground
artifact_observations.reasoning: The musical notation on the sheets is rendered as illegible scribbles and blob-like shapes rather than distinct notes and staves, a common AI artifact in rendering complex text/symbols.
The fingers appear slightly soft and fused with the instrument body, lacking sharp definition at the contact points.
Vertical lines in the background furniture waver and merge inconsistently, suggesting weak geometric coherence in the background.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the instrument and distinguish it from similar woodwinds like the contrabassoon or oboe.
To verify the physical connectivity of the instrument's joints and ensure the keys are properly attached to the wooden body without floating artifacts.
To rigorously quantify the legibility of the musical notation, which appeared gibberish in the initial scan.
To closely inspect the interaction between the musician's hands and the instrument for melting or anatomical errors.

focus_areas: Integrity of the metal keywork mechanism (are keys logically placed?)
Clarity of the wood grain texture vs. plastic/smooth artifacts
Anatomical correctness of fingers holding the instrument
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the sheet music; AI often fails to render valid musical notation. Also, check if the 'U-shape' of the bassoon is structurally sound even if viewed from the side—do the two parallel tubes look like they connect correctly at the bottom (boot joint)?
